positions.title: Security Software Engineer
positions.description: Working on a variety of problems in software supply-chain security, including build artifact attestation, CI/CD security, and artifact visibility across all stages of the development and deploy process.

positions.title: Security Software Engineer
positions.description: Worked to improve device safety, security, and privacy across the entire range of Oculus/Reality Labs hardware by building out the fundamentals: code signing, bootloader security, device identity, manufacturing controls, and so on.

positions.title: Applied Research Engineer
positions.description: As the fifth employee of a new (but growing!) startup, I did anything and everything, from writing FPGA software interfaces all the way up to cloud deployments. Along the way, I optimized bulk modular exponentiations, built out Spark processing pipelines, debugged database race conditions, designed RESTful APIs, created web UIs, and more.

positions.title: Applied Research Engineer
positions.description:
My team had the amazing job of imagining what the company might be doing in six months, then building it.

So I developed awesome prototypes of all sorts of ways to make encrypted data more usable and friendly: searching over encrypted documents, integrating Ionic's product into commercial services like Salesforce and Box, a generic system for protecting data in arbitrary applications, secret-sharing- and TPM-based methods for locking data to a specific computer, and more!

positions.title: Applied Research Mathematician
positions.description:
As part of a mathematics development program, I spent three years doing 6-9 month tours in offices across my agency. These covered a wide variety of technical work, including cryptography, signal processing, big data, front-end work, and software vulnerability research.

On graduation from the development program, I joined the Laboratory for Telecommunication Sciences as a security researcher.

positions.title: CS Staff
positions.description: I help maintain and improve the machines and software used by HMC's Computer Science department.

positions.title: Summer Research Student - Math
positions.description: I worked with another student on a project in algebraic geometry.  We used Sage to efficiently determine properties of families of hypersurfaces in certain Calabi-Yau varieties.  We also computed the Picard-Fuchs equation for a previously-unstudied family of hypersurfaces.  A paper based on this work is in progress, and a poster may be presented at the Joint Meeting of the AMS and MAA in January 2011.

positions.title: Intern
positions.description: I created several intricate spreadsheets to report on paper machine production data.  I also developed a protocol for working with a TAPIO paper analysis machine and software for automatically creating presentable reports on the data produced.

publications.title: Cooperative Search with Autonomous Vehicles in a 3D Aquatic Testbed
EC-OPRF: Oblivious Pseudorandom Functions using Elliptic Curves
